newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks close tad higher, hesitant.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks close tad higher, hesitant.

text.p: Argentine stocks closed fractionally higher for the second session running Tuesday and were seen keeping their undecided tone, dealers said.

"The market is looking very carefully at Wall Street and moving in a narrow range, while individual stocks are behaving selectively after the arrival of company results," said Leonardo Torres Barsati, senior analyst at Rio Research.
"The more volatile Wall Street gets, the more cautious we become," he added.
The blue-chip MerVal index added 0.3 percent to 729.29 while the broad market inched up 0.1 percent.
However, losers edged out winners 20 to 19 in the session and 25 issues closed flat.

Traders said the markets were bracing for Wednesday's U.S. producer price index and Thursday's consumer inflation. "That's why Wall Street eased today -- it needs some leeway after surging to record highs just in case the inflation numbers are not quite as good as expected," another trader said.
The bolsa's floor volume swelled to 27 million pesos from 16.3 million Monday, while over-the-counter turnover increased to 70.4 million pesos from 49.7 million Monday.

The biggest riser was textile and footwear firm Alpargatas, which surged 8.1 percent after rising 5.9 percent Monday despite reporting a quarterly loss of $39.4 million. Traders said the stock rose on news investment fund Newbridge Latin America would become one of the company's main stockholders after an $80 million negotiable bond subscription.
"They're betting long-term on Alpargatas," Barsati said.
Other top main-tier gainers were gas distributor Transportadora de Gas del Sur, which tacked on 0.8 percent, and Telefonica and oil giant YPF, both up 0.7 percent.
Losers were led by pulp and paper maker Celulosa and carmaker Sevel, which tumbled 9.9 percent and 5.4 percent, respectively.
